description: RBFS (Recursive Best-First Search) finds a cheapest path in memory linear in the search depth. It keeps only the current path and the siblings of its nodes. It goes down into the child with the smallest *backed-up* value `F` (the smallest `f` found below it so far), while that value stays within a bound: the smaller of the parent's bound and the second-best sibling's `F`. When a subtree exceeds its bound, it returns its smallest leaf value to the parent, which then switches to the best sibling. With an *admissible* heuristic (one that never overestimates) the path is optimal; the cost is that it regenerates subtrees when it comes back to them.
